extracted.intended_audience: national OGP members (governments), multi-stakeholder forums (MSFs), and civil society partners involved in designing and submitting OGP action plans
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for OGP national members and MSFs on co-creating, drafting, submitting, and managing OGP action plans and commitments in accordance with OGP Participation and Co-Creation Standards and OGP procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Requirement 3.1 — Publish co-creation timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The MSF where established, or the government where there is no MSF, publishes on the OGP website/webpage the co-creation timeline and overview of the opportunities for stakeholders to participate at least two weeks before the start of the action plan development process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRM assessment measures: Was the co-creation timeline with information on opportunities to participate available? Was the information made available two weeks before the start of the action plan development process? Also: publish timeline and maintain public OGP website to ensure transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Requirement 3.2 — Conduct outreach activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The MSF where established, or the government where there is no MSF, conducts outreach activities with stakeholders to raise awareness of OGP and opportunities to get involved in the development of the action plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRM assessment measure: Did the MSF or government conduct outreach activities with stakeholders to raise awareness of the OGP process? Outreach should aim to engage diverse stakeholders including citizens, civil society, government departments, subnational governments, parliament, academics, and the private sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Requirement 3.3 — Mechanism to gather stakeholder inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: The MSF where established, or the government where there is no MSF, develops a mechanism to gather inputs from a range of stakeholders during an appropriate period of time for the chosen mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRM assessment measures: Was there a mechanism in place to gather inputs from a range of stakeholders? Was the mechanism in place for an appropriate period of time? Use deliberative participation methods where possible to enable meaningful engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Requirement 4.1 — Document and publish reasoned response
rubrics_metrics.description: The MSF where established, or the government where there is no MSF, documents and reports back or publishes written feedback to stakeholders on how their contributions were considered during the development of the action plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRM assessment measures: Were contributions from stakeholders documented? Did the MSF or government provide a reasoned response to stakeholders and did it happen during the development of the action plan? Guidance: publish how suggestions were integrated or addressed to build transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-creation foundational expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-Creation as a Cornerstone: collaboration between government, civil society, and other stakeholders is central; participating governments must ensure that a diversity of voices can meaningfully participate and shape commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up a forum for ongoing dialogue, provide documentation on an online repository, purposefully design the co-creation process so stakeholders can provide ideas, feedback, identify priorities, and propose commitments. Early strategic planning (objectives, stakeholders, resources, timeline) is crucial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action plan length — two-year or four-year option
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries can decide to develop a two-year or a four-year action plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-year plans enable a shorter commitment cycle and potentially faster results; four-year plans allow extended time for more ambitious/complex reforms but require a mandatory refresh at the two-year mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-year action plan characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-year action plan: shorter commitment cycle focused on reforms that can be achieved and demonstrated within two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended for more limited or rapid-reform agendas; still must meet Participation and Co-Creation Standards and other OGP requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-year action plan — mandatory two-year refresh
rubrics_metrics.description: Four-year action plans must conduct a mandatory refresh at the two-year mark to review progress, assess context, and make adjustments so the plan remains relevant and effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refresh process includes: review of progress (identify gaps/challenges), outreach (communicate results and solicit feedback), revision (modify/add commitments), feedback (publish reasoned response), and submission (refreshed plan due no later than six months after the two-year mark). Additional requirements: publish a timeline of refresh steps at least two weeks before review; share results from public consultations; IRM provides a Midterm Review assessing the refresh and any refreshed/new commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery windows and end dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries may submit their action plan during one of two delivery windows which determine the fixed official end date: End date of 30 June or End date of 31 December.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 30 June window: submit between 1 January and 31 August; 31 December window: submit between 1 July and 28 February. If submitted in overlapping months (Jan, Feb, Jul, Aug), country must explicitly choose whether the plan concludes on 30 June or 31 December.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline for consecutive action plans and no extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: After concluding an action plan, a country must deliver its next action plan within one year counted from the end date of the previous plan. No extensions are allowed beyond these deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support Unit recommends starting co-creation of the next plan during the final months of implementing the current one to ensure continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements to OGP
rubrics_metrics.description: Action plans must be submitted via email to the relevant lead OGP staff member and must be submitted in the country’s administrative language and in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OGP staff will acknowledge receipt and publish the plan on the OGP website. Submitting in English allows the IRM to begin assessment. Once submitted, the plan is considered final (cannot submit a draft); drafts may be shared informally with Support Unit for feedback prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and handling of delays
rubrics_metrics.description: If a government does not deliver a new action plan within one year after completion of their previous plan, they will be officially late and considered to have acted contrary to process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support Unit will send a letter noting the delay (copied to Criteria and Standards subcommittee) and publish the letter on the country page. Countries late must deliver by 30 June or 31 December of the subsequent year to avoid acting contrary to process again and potential Procedural Review under OGP Membership Accountability Mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments during implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries may modify or remove commitments or milestones within one year of the action plan’s submission. Countries may introduce new commitments during implementation provided all milestones are completed before the action plan’s scheduled end date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated action plans detailing changes must be submitted to the OGP Support Unit in English and the country’s administrative language. IRM Action Plan Reviews assess the initial plan; IRM Results Reports assess the most recent formally submitted version. For four-year plans, the IRM will assess new or significantly amended commitments at the midpoint Midterm Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key moments of co-creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-creation consists of several key moments: planning for co-creation; stakeholder outreach and engagement; action plan formulation; feedback and reasoned response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning includes objectives, stakeholders, resources, timeline; outreach engages diverse stakeholders and uses mechanisms to gather input; formulation transforms input into concrete commitments using the OGP commitment template; feedback phase explains how contributions were considered to build trust and strengthen collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action plan content — Introduction section
rubrics_metrics.description: The Introduction should briefly explain national/local context, why open government is important, outline governance reform priorities, identify major issues the action plan will address, and provide justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guiding questions include: long-term vision for open government; medium-term goals; how this action plan contributes to goals; what major issues are being addressed and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action plan content — Open Government Efforts to Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief narrative of key open government initiatives and accomplishments to date, especially collaborative efforts with civil society, and explain how the new action plan builds on previous plans and related efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guiding questions: achievements to date, how collaboration shaped reforms, which previous commitments were achieved or not and why, and how the new plan builds on past efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action plan content — Development process documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the government collaborated with civil society and stakeholders to plan, structure, conduct outreach, formulate commitments, and provide feedback; expressly note compliance with OGP Participation and Co-Creation Standards and minimum participation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guiding questions: How was timeline developed? Who was involved? How were inputs considered? How were outreach activities conducted? What spaces were used for collaboration? How was problem definition and solution identification carried out? How was the reasoned response provided?

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitments — promote ambitious reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Action plans should 'Promote ambitious reforms that stretch government practice beyond their current baseline' and aim for binding and institutionalized changes that can be 'game changers' for practices, policies, or institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRM assesses ambition via its 'Potential for Results' indicator. Ambitious commitments often require multi-year timelines or institutional changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitments — align with OGP principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Each commitment should advance at least one OGP principle: Transparency, Citizen Participation, or Public Accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Transparency commitments enable proactive/reactive disclosure or improve right to information; Citizen Participation commitments create or improve participatory mechanisms and enable inclusion; Public Accountability commitments create or improve mechanisms to hold officials answerable and involve public participation rather than purely internal processes. IRM assesses relevance via 'Open Government Lens' indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitments — prioritize reforms (5–15 high-quality commitments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Action plans comprising 5-15 high-quality commitments spread over multiple themes are more effective than plans with a large number of less ambitious commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on fewer, well-scoped, high-impact commitments rather than many low-ambition items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitments — SMART criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitments should be SMART: Specific, Measurable, Answerable, Relevant, Time-bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific: clear problem, activities, expected outcomes. Measurable: define milestones and outcomes that can be tracked/verified. Answerable: identify lead implementing agency and supporting stakeholders. Relevant: align with OGP principles. Time-bound: set deadlines and milestones. IRM assesses clarity and objective verifiability via its 'Verifiability' indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment Template — Problem definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem definition should detail who is affected, where, how, when they are affected, when the problem started and how long it has persisted; include causes and root causes and may use analytical tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A thorough problem definition supports realistic design of activities, milestones, and measures of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment Template — Commitment description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe what has been done so far to solve the problem, the proposed solution, how it differs from previous efforts, how it will solve (fully or partially), and the desired results including outputs and changes in capacities, behaviors, systems, and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the commitment builds on or diverges from past approaches and state the intended outcomes clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment Template — Commitment analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the proposed commitment will promote transparency, foster accountability, and improve participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie the commitment explicitly to one or more OGP principles and explain the mechanism by which the commitment will create open-government effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment Template — Commitment planning (milestones, outputs, stakeholders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include milestones, expected outputs (objectively verifiable results), expected completion date, and identify the lead and supporting stakeholders involved in implementing the commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Milestones should showcase a series of actions or events leading to the result; expected outputs should be concrete and verifiable; specify coordinating and supporting agencies and civil society roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment Template — Open Government Challenge relevance (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitments can be designated as submissions for the Open Government Challenge if they meet criteria such as corresponding to one of the ten Challenge areas; OGP makes the final decision based on four criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge submissions are possible inside or outside an action plan; see Open Gov Challenge page for details. OGP decides on acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment Template — recommended use conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The standardized commitment template is intended for more advanced stages of planning rather than brainstorming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most effective when problems are well-defined, potential solutions have been thoroughly discussed/evaluated/prioritized, and there is a clear vision of what the commitment will look like to allow planning of milestones, objectives, and theory of change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoned response as predictor of success
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing a reasoned response to stakeholder input is highly correlated with ambition, completion, and early results in commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence from IRM reports shows reasoned responses are the best predictor of strong action plans; documenting why ideas were included or excluded helps ensure accountability, mitigate disengagement, and overcome resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: MSF/government operational responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: MSFs (or government where no MSF) are expected to lead co-creation planning, publish timelines, conduct outreach, maintain public document repositories, communicate review results, and publish reasoned responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During four-year refreshes MSFs should conduct review of progress, solicit feedback, revise plans through consultation, and publish how stakeholder contributions were considered; timeline of refresh steps must be published at least two weeks before review process begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRM assessment and indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: The Independent Reporting Mechanism (IRM) will assess compliance with minimum requirements and evaluate commitments using indicators such as 'Potential for Results', 'Open Government Lens', and 'Verifiability'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRM Action Plan Reviews assess the initial plan; IRM Results Reports use the most recent formally submitted version; for four-year plans IRM provides a Midterm Review assessing refreshed or new commitments and overall implementation progress. Submit plans in English so IRM can begin research/assessment.
